text:
alex: Heads-up — running long-context loadtests and seeing steady memory growth in the KV-store on Dedicated pools. Hosted looks stable, Private (on-prem) shows a different pattern.

nina: Can you paste the flame/heap snapshot? short traces help.

alex: Pushed a sampling trace to /bench/results/kv-longctx/341987 — key excerpts below.

alex: ```
kv_pages_total: 1.9G
kv_pages_in_use: 1.74G -> 1.86G over 3h
evict_ops/sec: 0.2 -> 0.8
swap_activity: 0
pagewalks: increased by 18%
backpressure_ms: 0 -> 12ms
```

omar: Interesting that hosted is flat. What differs in config? Dedicated has `kv_reclaim_target=0.7` vs hosted `0.85`? Also Dedicated nodes on GCP have default hugepage/off and different kernel (5.15 vs 6.1) IIRC.

maya: Private runs on A100s with NUMA interleave policy set to local_mem — we saw slot residency skew before. Could be NUMA-induced fragmentation.

sara: Any batching deltas? small batches can increase slot churn if partial KV reads/writes happen frequently.

alex: Batching windows: Hosted=3ms, Dedicated=1ms, Private=0ms (server tuned for low latency). I think the tiny window on Dedicated/Private -> lots of tiny KV touchpoints, causing hotter tail and more frequent soft-evicts.

nina: Can you try bumping `batch_fill_timeout_ms` to 4-5ms on a canary Dedicated pool and re-run the long ctx test? If bandwidth holds, it should reduce churn and amortize page scans.

alex: Did a micro-run on a Dedicated canary with `batch_fill_timeout_ms=5` and `kv_reclaim_target=0.78`. After 30m: growth plateaued (1.81G -> 1.82G) and evict_ops/sec dropped 0.8 -> 0.3. Latency tail +0.7ms p99 but throughput unchanged.

omar: That suggests batching heuristics are doing most of the heavy lifting. Kernel selection still matters: older kernels on Dedicated don't support our new `madvise(MERGE)` hint which reduced fragmentation in hosted 6.x kernels.

maya: For Private onprem, NVLINK+NUMA causes different allocation alignments, we saw page alignment mismatch with jemalloc that caused page splitting. Did you test enabling `--hugepages=on`?

alex: Enabled hugepages on one Private node. Memory growth rate reduced but we saw higher initial resident set due to larger page granularity. Evict pattern changed from many small-ish evict ops to fewer larger ones.

sara: Tradeoff seems clear: tiny batch windows => low latency but more KV churn and fragmentation; larger pages/hugepages => lower fragmentation but coarser reclaim spikes.

infra-bot: deploy-canary: Canary deploy queued on pool dedicated-us-west-2-kv-canary. ID: dply-98b4

nina: For next steps: 1) run 24h canary with `batch_fill_timeout_ms=5` on Dedicated 2) test madvise(MERGE) backport on Dedicated kernel 3) test hugepages toggles on Private node 4) add KV slot residency histogram to perf dashboard.

omar: I'll add a small sampling profiler to collect per-tenant slot residency and page fragmentation histogram (low overhead). Will use `perf mem` sampling + our aggregators.

alex: Filed tickets: INF-7123 (canary + metrics), INF-7124 (kernel madvise backport), INF-7125 (hugepages experiment). Pinning owners: nina, omar, maya.

sara: Also consider a transient prefetch/warmup for long-contexts: when long ctx detected, pre-warm next N prefixes to reduce on-demand page faults.

alex: Good idea — I prototyped a prefix-warm that reduced pagewalks by ~30% in a short run. Will attach patch to INF-7123.

nina: Great. If canary looks good after 24h we can roll to Dedicated. Keep hosted configs unchanged for now.

alex: OK, will kick off canary and post updates in this thread. Thanks y'all :thumbsup:
